rationale: C04 plausibly supplied the principal drafting template. It presents the same disability-payment tax issue and follows essentially the same factual and argumentative sequence: the taxpayer reported disability payments as income despite contrary appellate authority; the Supreme Court later held those payments excludable; the refund claim was rejected as untimely; the limitations period is defended as necessary for finality; and individual relief is rejected as discriminatory and precedent-setting. The child adapts C04 to Mrs. Estes, two tax years, and adds a discussion of intervening general legislation. C01 is closely related factually but reaches a different rationale because general relief was available to those taxpayers. C18 shares much of the limitations-policy language and structure but concerns a different underlying tax error.

shared_material.child_excerpt: At the time the taxpayer filed these returns, the Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit had held that such disability payments were excludable from gross income, although the Internal Revenue Service had ruled to the contrary.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: At the time the taxpayer filed his return for 1952, the Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit had held that such disability payments were excludable from gross income, although the Internal Revenue Service had ruled to the contrary.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim distinctive factual and legal framing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On April 1, 1957, the United States Supreme Court decided that disability payments of the type here in question were excludable from gross income.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: On April 1, 1957, the United States Supreme Court decided that disability payments of the type received by the taxpayer were excludable from gross income.
shared_material.explanation: The same operative sentence is reused with only a minor adaptation to the claimant.

shared_material.child_excerpt: These claims were rejected because filed after the expiration of the 3-year period of limitations prescribed by law for the filing of such claims.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This claim was rejected because it was filed after the expiration of the three-year period of limitations prescribed by law for the filing of such claims.
shared_material.explanation: Near-verbatim description of the administrative disposition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which the Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential in order to achieve finality in tax administration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which the Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential in order to achieve finality in tax administration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: to grant special relief in this case, where a refund was not claimed in the time and manner prescribed by law, would be to discriminate against such other similarly situated taxpayers and to create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To grant special relief in this case, therefore, where a refund was not claimed in the time and manner prescribed by law, would constitute a discrimination against other similarly situated taxpayers and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim concluding rationale applying the same administrative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Under the circumstances, therefore, I am constrained to withhold my approval from the bill.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Under the circumstances, therefore, I am constrained to withhold my approval of the bill.
shared_material.explanation: Matching conclusion, reinforcing the broader sequence of shared drafting.
